failure_summary.description: Some trajectories left results unsaved or made duplicate/bare calls despite existing assign-and-save and no-duplicate rules.
Agents missed pending requests, failed to apply new constraints to suitable cached results, or used unrelated results and operations.
Agents failed to search both legs of an explicit round trip or proceeded to seek dates already supplied in context.
Agents mis-mapped a state abbreviation to city and treated an exact departure time as a one-sided lower bound.

patch.reasoning: Most observed failures are already directly covered by the skill's persistence, cache-follow-up, date, and location rules, so repeating them would not patch a gap. The flight-time guidance does not explicitly distinguish an exact time from a one-sided bound; clarifying that distinction addresses the remaining supported ambiguity.

edits.target: - For a one-sided flight-time bound, complete the range to the day boundary: “before X” uses `["12:00 AM", X]`, and “after X” uses `[X, "11:59 PM"]`, preserving the stated AM/PM value.
edits.content: When the user specifies one exact flight time as “at X” without a range or one-sided qualifier, use `[X, X]` for the corresponding time field; do not interpret it as an “after X” bound.
